belief: If I had enough faith, I wouldn't be poor.
origins: Messages that promise wealth to the faithful are common in some preaching, books, and broadcasts. When someone who prays and gives still struggles, the teaching leaves only one conclusion: my faith must be lacking. Guilt follows, and the pain of poverty is joined by spiritual shame.
teaches: James writes, “Has not God chosen the poor of this world to be rich in faith and to inherit the kingdom He promised those who love Him?” Paul describes the Macedonian churches: “In the terrible ordeal they suffered, their abundant joy and deep poverty overflowed into rich generosity.” Paul also says, “I know how to live humbly, and I know how to abound… to having plenty and having need.” The heroes of faith were not always rich. Faith is trust in God, not a payment method for a comfortable life.
self_statements: If I believed more, God would provide.
I am not praying hard enough.
I must be doing something wrong.
Other believers have more because they have more faith.
My poverty is my fault spiritually.
errors: Blaming my faith for circumstances with many causes.
Believing faith works like a formula for money.
Seeing faith as either producing wealth or failing.
Feeling guilty and concluding my faith is lacking.
questions: Who taught me that faith produces wealth?
Which people in the Bible had great faith and little money?
What did Paul say about learning to be content in every situation?
What is faith in Scripture really about?
What other causes could contribute to my financial situation?
What would it look like to trust God in this, without guilt?
truth: Faith is trusting God, not purchasing wealth. Many faithful people in Scripture knew need. My struggle is not proof of weak faith, and I can keep trusting God with joy and sensible steps.
hw_truths: Faith is not a formula for wealth.
God chose the poor to be rich in faith.
Paul learned to live in plenty and in need.
My poverty is not a spiritual failure.
I can trust God in every circumstance.
God is with me when the fields are empty.
log: Each week, write one way you trusted God this week, whatever your circumstances.
actions: Write names from Scripture or your life who trusted God in need.
Write a sentence that says what faith really is.
Write one practical step you can take about your finances.
prayer: Lord, I have wondered if my faith is not enough. Teach me what real faith is. Help me trust You in plenty and in need, and release the guilt that is not from You. Amen.
hw_questions: Who taught me faith produces wealth?
Who in Scripture trusted God in need?
What other causes affect my finances?
What practical step can I take?
How can I trust God today?
name_example: Sarah can write: “God has chosen the poor to be rich in faith, so my need is not proof my faith is weak.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “If I had enough faith, I wouldn't be poor.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
